text:
anya: Heads up — after last night's autoshrink + kernel-selection merge I'm seeing repeat OOMs on a subset of longctx jobs. First noticed on canary pool-7, ~10% failure rate.

morgan: ugh. which change exactly? autoshrink touched heaplet free paths and the kernel router changed fallback ordering. could be an interaction.

anya: stack: model=llama-70b, seq=4096, batch=2 (burst). Logs show allocator rejecting large slab requests then rapid heaplet churn: 
```
OOM: failed allocate 4194304 bytes in heaplet 3
heaplet_status: used=1.9GB free=120MB peak=2.1GB
stack: runtime::alloc_slowpath -> heaplet::reserve -> kv_cache::warmup
```

raul: do we have perf profiles? maybe kernel choice increased memcpy/fragmentation.

anya: attached pprof for the failing run (summarized): most time in kv_cache rebalance + mmap churn, but the interesting bit is frequent small frees followed by large allocs -> fragmentation.

morgan: CI also flagged a mem regression on the same PR yesterday: perf CI + memory smoke on longctx. ci-bot: flagged as +18% peak RSS on long-seq tests.

ci-bot: (automated) regression: job longctx_integration/seq4096 increased peak_memory from 7.3GB to 8.6GB on PR #4123.

anya: confirmed locally with repro script: toggling the kernel router to previous ordering removes the OOM. So kernel selection seems to affect allocation patterns.

raul: good bisect candidate. can you share the minimal repro? I can try git-bisect between autoshrink merge and kernel-router reorder.

anya: repro: ./scripts/run_longctx.sh --model llama-70b --seq 4096 --batch 2 --prefetch on. I'll drop perf artifacts in the thread.

morgan: quick mitigation: hold rollout to canary and add a guard in the router to use prior selection when seq>=2048 until we root cause. I'll open a rollback PR if bisect shows kernel change is culprit.

anya: started bisect locally: first bad commit is 3 commits after autoshrink merge but before routing rewrite, which is odd. there might be a subtle allocator change in autoshrink causing sensitivity to kernel order.

raul: ok i'll run bisect matrix on pool-7 with both prefetch on/off and seq sweep 1024/2048/4096. will post results.

infra-bot: (note) pool-7 canary capacity increased for debug. ephemeral logs will be retained for 48h.

morgan: also adding a CI regression gate: require peak_mem difference < +5% for longctx smoke when merging kernel/router or allocator changes. failing builds will prevent rollout.

anya: action items: 1) raul to finish bisect and confirm offending commit; 2) morgan to open temporary router-guard + CI mem gate; 3) anya to collect more heap snapshots and fragmentation histograms.

raul: running bisect now, will ping with first failing commit id (expect ~30-45m). thanks. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
